subject: Runtime third-party tooling clause — cross-functional signoff needed
messages:
From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@healthbridge.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@healthbridge.com
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: HealthBridge - DPA redline (runtime tooling / subprocessors)

Marcus — attaching our redline for the DPA. Two items we flagged that we need clarity on before legal can sign: 1) the runtime third-party tooling clause (they added a paragraph that would allow Redwood to route runtime requests to monitoring/observability vendors that may see request payload metadata) and 2) an expanded subprocessor list for analytics/telemetry exports.

Short ask: can you confirm whether those runtime routing paths include any PII or model input/outputs, and what controls (encryption/KMS, ephemeral keys, KV cache residency) you apply? We put suggested language in Exhibit C and highlighted an example carveout we need to accept if you cannot guarantee non-visibility.

Attachment: HealthBridge_DPA_Redline_v3.docx (docx)
Attachment: Exhibit-C-runtime-subprocessors.xlsx (xlsx)

If you prefer a quick sync today we can jump on a 20-min call.

— Sanjay
Legal, HealthBridge
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthBridge - DPA redline (runtime tooling / subprocessors)

Thanks Sanjay — received and thanks for the clear highlights. I skimmed the redline and attached spreadsheet. I want to loop in product and security to confirm our exact runtime behavior before we propose edits back.

Olga / Karthik / Priya — quick context: HealthBridge is asking for stronger guarantees that runtime third-party tooling (monitoring, APM, analytics) will not have access to model inputs/outputs. Their redline proposes: (a) a ban on sending request payloads to third parties unless explicitly agreed, and (b) a broad telemetry subprocessor list in Exhibit C that includes our monitoring vendor and an analytics partner. They also request an explicit guarantee that KV cache snapshots or prefix caching will never be exported.

My immediate asks:
- Olga: are any of our runtime observability paths sending de-duplicated or sampled payloads outside the cluster today? If so, what fields are included (headers/metadata only vs. content)?
- Karthik / Priya: from product POV, can we accept a limited carveout for latency/health telemetry (token counts, error rates, sampling ids) but not payloads? Is there an operational impact if we restrict analytics vendor access to aggregated telemetry only?

Sanjay — propose we aim to return a consolidated redline + short explanation by Tue 16 Jun. If product/security need more time we can ask for a brief extension.

Marcus
Director, Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthBridge - DPA redline (runtime tooling / subprocessors)

Marcus / Sanjay — technical note from runtime/security operations below. I copied Karthik for product implications.

Summary:
- Observability: Our APM and metrics pipeline collects request-level metadata (request_id, timestamp, route, token_count, latency, error_code). We do NOT forward full request or response bodies to external monitoring vendors in the default pipeline.
- Sampling: We have a debug sampling path used for customer support that can capture deidentified prompts or short context when a customer explicitly enables debug logging; that path is gated behind an opt-in flag and access controls.
- KV cache: KV cache snapshots are stored encrypted at rest and are not exported to external vendors. We do allow periodic aggregated cache hit-rate metrics to be exported.
- Third-party tooling: Some internal tooling (anomaly detection/feature telemetry) runs in a partner-managed analytics account; those jobs receive aggregated telemetry data only.

Concrete proposal for redline language:
1) Accept clause that prohibits export of raw model inputs/outputs to subprocessors without explicit written consent.
2) Provide an allowed-exception list limited to aggregated runtime telemetry (token counts, route-level metrics, error rates) and service-level alerts necessary for operational health.
3) Add an explicit opt-in path for debug sampling that requires customer consent and logs an audit event.

Open items: what counts as "aggregated" vs "sampled" in legal language. Karthik — product will need to sign off on the definition and any UX constraints (opt-in flow, retention windows).

— Olga
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthBridge - DPA redline (runtime tooling / subprocessors)

Thanks for the clear breakdown. Product position and next steps below.

Position: we can accept the technical proposal Olga outlined with the following product guardrails:
- "Aggregated telemetry" = time-bucketed, route-level metrics (no per-request identifiers that would let HealthBridge or a subprocessor reconstruct request-level content). Examples: per-minute token_count_sum, error_rate_pct, avg_latency_ms.
- "Sampling" for debug: must be explicit customer opt-in from Console or API; samples stored only for 14 days by default and accessible to customer and authorized support staff; samples are flagged and searchable only by sample id (no cross-tenant correlation).
- Exhibit C: prune the subprocessor list to include only vendors that handle aggregated metrics and monitoring alerts; remove any vendor that would require payload-level exports.

Operational impact: requiring aggregated-only exports means we will need to change one partner job to drop per-request identifiers (2 sprint effort) and update our onboarding docs for customers who want debug sampling. We estimate go-live of the updated partner job in ~6 weeks.

My ask to legal (Sanjay): if we incorporate the allowed-exception language and the opt-in debug flow, will HealthBridge accept the Exhibit C pruned list + a 6-week remediation timeline? If yes, Marcus / Olga — please confirm the wording and the KV cache non-export guarantee, and I will prepare a short product note for the counter-redline.

— Karthik
Staff Product Manager, Redwood Inference
